newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurdish strongman in Turkey for U.S. talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish strongman in Turkey for U.S. talks.

text.p: Baghdad-backed Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani arrived in Turkey on Wednesday, ahead of his first talks with U.S. officials since he took control of northern Iraq, effectively ending U.S. operations there.
Witnesses said Barzani was driven through the Habur border crossing in a black Mercedes car accompanied by half a dozen vehicles carrying guards and aides.
A Turkish military helicopter flew over the convoy as it headed for the southeastern city of Diyarbakir, they said.
Barzani, head of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), was to hold talks in Ankara with Robert Pelletreau, U.S. assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs.
A KDP official said Barzani would hold talks with Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller on Wednesday and probably meet Pelletreau later in the day or on Thursday.
"The timings of the meetings will become clear later," the group's Ankara spokesman Faik Nerweyi told Reuters.
Barzani's forces joined with Iraqi troops and tanks to capture the Kurdish city of Arbil from a rival militia last month, prompting U.S. missile strikes on targets in southern Iraq.

However, Washington pulled back its military, aid and intelligence operations from Iraq, fearful that Barzani's new ties to the central government in Baghdad would put U.S. personnel and their local staffs at risk.
An evacuation of hundreds of Kurdish families linked to U.S. efforts in the predominantly Kurdish north undercut Washington's ability to influence events in the remote region.
